title: Lower the Ridge, Not the Valleys

scenes.tts: Can an enzyme make an impossible reaction happen? Or can it only make a possible one fast? Start with a reaction your cells need to make RNA.
scenes.visual: THE WORLD (carried through the whole film): a side-on landscape that fills the frame width (x -6.2..6.2) and about 65% of its height. Its ground line is ONE computed curve, G(x) = s(x) + H*exp(-(x/1.1)^2), where s(x) = -1.3 - 0.7*tanh(x/1.6) steps smoothly from the LEFT VALLEY floor at y -0.6 down to the RIGHT VALLEY floor at y -2.0, and H is the Gaussian ridge amplitude (start H = 4.2, ridge top near y 2.9). A small 'schematic' tag (TEXT, 28) sits bottom-right whenever the landscape is on screen: heights are not to scale. COLOR MAP: YELLOW substrate (dots in the left valley), GREEN product (right valley), RED the high uncatalyzed pass, TEAL the enzyme and the lowered pass, PURPLE the transition state, GOLD the enzyme's grip. Labels size 30+, full opacity, at most 5 words, at most 6 things on screen. No molecular structures anywhere: dots, blobs, curves, chips. NO fade from black: the landscape is already drawn and alive. Eight YELLOW dots jiggle in the left valley (small random drift by updater, each bouncing off the slopes, none ever reaching the top). On 'impossible reaction' a RED arrow tries to climb from the low RIGHT valley up into the higher LEFT valley, stalls halfway and a RED '?' badge (40) pops on it. On 'possible one fast' a YELLOW arrow traces the downhill route from the left valley over the ridge into the right valley, and a TEAL '?' badge (40) pops beside the ridge top. On 'Start with a reaction' both arrows and badges fade; a chip 'one step toward RNA' (TEXT, 30) settles over the left valley while the dots keep jiggling.
scenes.narration: Can an enzyme make an impossible reaction happen? Or can it only make a possible one fast? Start with a reaction your cells need to make RNA.

scenes.visual: Do not cut away: the landscape stays at 25% opacity, dots still jiggling. Over it: BIOCHEMISTRYPEDIA (TEAL), the title 'Lower the Ridge, Not the Valleys' (TITLE_FONT 54) and a GOLD rule. Title out in the last 0.4 s; landscape back to full opacity.

scenes.tts: On its own, this step is painfully slow. Half the molecules would take seventy eight million years to react. With its enzyme, the step is done in milliseconds.
scenes.caption: On its own, this step is painfully slow. Half the molecules would take 78 million years to react. With its enzyme, the step is done in milliseconds.
scenes.visual: The landscape shrinks into the upper 55% of the frame (same curve, same dots, still jiggling). Below it a LOG TIME AXIS draws in from left to right as the first sentence is spoken (x -5.5..5.5, y -2.9; ticks every 3 powers of ten of seconds from 10^-3 s to 10^16 s, labelled only at 'a second', 'a year', 'a million years', size 28; positions computed from log10 of seconds). On 'Half the molecules' a RED marker slides from the left end along the axis, the slide easing slower as it goes, and parks at 78 million years (log10 of 78e6 x 3.156e7 s = 15.4); the label 'half-life: 78 million years' (RED, 30) appears above it. While the marker slides, exactly half of the eight YELLOW dots blink (they are the half that would react). On 'With its enzyme' a TEAL marker drops onto the axis at 'milliseconds' (10^-2 s) with the label 'with enzyme: milliseconds' (TEAL, 30), and the gap between the two markers fills with a TEAL double arrow.
scenes.narration: On its own, this step is painfully slow. Half the molecules would take 78 million years to react. With its enzyme, the step is done in milliseconds.

scenes.tts: That is a speed-up of about ten to the seventeen. So could an enzyme that strong push a reaction uphill? No. To see why, split one question into two.
scenes.caption: That is a speed-up of about 10¹⁷. So could an enzyme that strong push a reaction uphill? No. To see why, split one question into two.
scenes.visual: On 'speed-up' the TEAL double arrow from s02 lifts off the axis and becomes a counter chip 'speed-up about 10^17' (TEAL, 34) that docks in the top-right corner, where it stays for the film. The time axis folds away downward. On 'push a reaction uphill' the landscape grows back to full size and a single YELLOW dot in the right valley tries to roll up the long slope toward the higher left valley, slides back down, tries again. On 'No' a RED cross stamps over its path. On 'split one question into two' two empty chip outlines appear at the top-left and top-centre, one labelled 'which way?' and one 'how fast?' (TEXT, 30); the dots go on jiggling in the left valley.
scenes.narration: That is a speed-up of about 10¹⁷. So could an enzyme that strong push a reaction uphill? No. To see why, split one question into two.

scenes.tts: Which valley is lower decides which way the reaction runs. That is thermodynamics, delta G. How high the ridge is decides how fast. That is kinetics.
scenes.caption: Which valley is lower decides which way the reaction runs. That is thermodynamics, ΔG. How high the ridge is decides how fast. That is kinetics.
scenes.visual: Just before 'Which valley' the two valley floors glow: the left floor YELLOW with label 'substrate' (YELLOW, 30), the right floor GREEN with label 'product' (GREEN, 30). A GREEN vertical bracket grows downward from the left floor's height to the right floor's height before 'delta G'; on 'delta G' the bracket gets its label 'ΔG' (GREEN, 34) and the 'which way?' chip fills GREEN. A RED vertical bracket grows from the left floor up to the ridge top just before 'How high the ridge', tracing the climb; on 'how fast' the 'how fast?' chip fills RED. The dots keep jiggling at the bottom of the left valley.
scenes.narration: Which valley is lower decides which way the reaction runs. That is thermodynamics, ΔG. How high the ridge is decides how fast. That is kinetics.

scenes.tts: That climb is the activation energy, delta G double dagger. At the very top sits the transition state. Its bonds are partly breaking and forming, and it lasts femtoseconds.
scenes.visual: The RED bracket gets its label 'ΔG‡' (RED, 34) on 'activation energy'. Just before 'transition state' the camera eases in on the ridge top (zoom so the top third of the ridge fills 60% of the frame height; the valleys leave the edges). A round YELLOW dot climbs the slope and stretches into a PURPLE oval exactly at the summit; on 'transition state' its label (PURPLE, 30) appears. On 'bonds are partly' the oval stretches a little further and two chips, 'bond breaking' and 'bond forming' (PURPLE, 28), appear at its ends (words only, nothing drawn inside the oval: no structure). On 'femtoseconds' the oval wobbles on the summit for a beat, then tips and rolls down the right slope, turning GREEN as it goes. Zoom back out to the whole landscape as it lands.
scenes.narration: That climb is the activation energy, delta G double dagger. At the very top sits the transition state. Its bonds are partly breaking and forming, and it lasts femtoseconds.

scenes.tts: Here is the whole idea. An enzyme lowers the ridge. It never moves the valleys. It opens a lower pass over the same ridge, still a highest point, just lower.
scenes.visual: On 'Here is the whole idea' everything except the landscape, the dots and the counter chip fades. Before 'lowers the ridge' a TEAL copy of the ground curve peels away from the RED one and its ridge starts sinking smoothly (H animated from 4.2 down to 1.8, the curve recomputed every frame); the old high pass stays as a RED dashed curve. Before 'never moves the valleys' two small TEAL pins drop onto the left and right valley floors; on the words, the floors flash and the TEAL and RED curves coincide exactly there. Before 'a lower pass' a TEAL label 'lower pass' (30) settles on the new top; on 'still a highest point' a PURPLE dot marks that top. Through the whole scene dots start crossing the TEAL pass, a few per second, and dropping into the right valley; the RED dashed pass gets none.
scenes.narration: Here is the whole idea. An enzyme lowers the ridge. It never moves the valleys. It opens a lower pass over the same ridge, still a highest point, just lower.

scenes.tts: A little lower buys a lot of speed. At twenty five degrees, every five point seven kilojoules per mole taken off makes it ten times faster.
scenes.caption: A little lower buys a lot of speed. At 25 °C, every 5.7 kJ/mol taken off makes it ten times faster.
scenes.visual: Carry the landscape (RED dashed high pass, TEAL lowered pass). Rebuild the TEAL pass at full height H = 4.2 for this scene. A GAUGE appears at the right edge: a vertical bar labelled 'times faster' (TEAL, 28) with a counter beneath reading 'x1'. On 'every five point seven' the TEAL ridge steps down in five equal steps of 5.7 kJ/mol (schematic height per step), and with each step the counter is computed as 10^(drop/5.7): x10, x100, x1,000, x10,000, x100,000. Each step lands on a soft click and the stream of dots over the pass visibly thickens. A chip '5.7 kJ/mol = ten times' (TEAL, 30) sits beside the steps.
scenes.narration: A little lower buys a lot of speed. At 25 °C, every 5.7 kJ/mol taken off makes it ten times faster.

scenes.tts: Take off about ninety seven, and you reach that ten to the seventeen. Now flip the trip, from product back to substrate.
scenes.caption: Take off about 97, and you reach that 10¹⁷. Now flip the trip, from product back to substrate.
scenes.visual: On 'about ninety seven' the TEAL ridge keeps stepping down fast to its s06 height, the counter racing up and stopping at 'x 10^17' as it meets the corner chip 'speed-up about 10^17', which pulses once. A chip '97 kJ/mol' (TEAL, 30) sits on the drop. On 'flip the trip' the gauge and chips fade; one GREEN dot in the right valley glows and a GREEN arrow traces the reverse route, from the product valley up over the TEAL pass and back to the left valley.
scenes.narration: Take off about 97, and you reach that 10¹⁷. Now flip the trip, from product back to substrate.

scenes.tts: Say the enzyme speeds the forward trip a millionfold. Watch both arrows cross the same lowered top. What happens to the backward trip?
scenes.visual: Two arrows over the TEAL pass: a YELLOW forward arrow (left to right) labelled 'x 1,000,000' (YELLOW, 32), and a GREEN backward arrow (right to left) labelled 'x ?' (GREEN, 40). On 'Watch both arrows' they each cross the same TEAL top. On 'backward trip' a question card slides up in the lower third: 'Backward: faster, slower, unchanged?' (TEXT, 34). The dots keep crossing slowly both ways.
scenes.narration: Say the enzyme speeds the forward trip a millionfold. Watch both arrows cross the same lowered top. What happens to the backward trip?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. The question card and the 'x ?' label stay on screen. Near silence. Gentle motion only: dots drift in both valleys, a few cross the TEAL pass in each direction, the '?' breathes (scale 1.0 to 1.06 and back).

scenes.tts: Also a millionfold. Counted from the two valleys, both trips cross the same lowered top. So their ratio, the equilibrium constant, stays the same.
scenes.visual: Card gone. On 'Also a millionfold' the 'x ?' turns into 'x 1,000,000' (GREEN, 32). On 'the two valleys' the TEAL pins on both floors flash again. On 'the same lowered top' two brackets grow at once from each floor up to the TEAL top, the forward one YELLOW and the backward one GREEN, both ending at the same PURPLE point. On 'their ratio' the two 'x 1,000,000' labels slide together into a fraction and cancel into a chip 'Keq: unchanged' (TEXT, 34).
scenes.narration: Also a millionfold. Counted from the two valleys, both trips cross the same lowered top. So their ratio, the equilibrium constant, stays the same.

scenes.tts: The enzyme reaches the same equilibrium, only sooner. It cannot push a reaction uphill. If the far valley is higher, the net reaction runs the other way.
scenes.visual: On 'same equilibrium' a split counter appears under the valleys showing how many dots sit in each valley; dots flow fast over the TEAL pass until the counts settle at a ratio, and a RED dashed-pass ghost run beside it (small inset, top-left, same landscape) settles at the SAME ratio, just later (both computed from the same two valley heights; the inset is labelled 'no enzyme: same end, later', 28). Inset fades. On 'If the far valley is higher' the right valley floor rises smoothly above the left one (the whole curve recomputed, both passes follow); on 'runs the other way' the dot flow reverses and most dots pour back into the left valley.
scenes.narration: The enzyme reaches the same equilibrium, only sooner. It cannot push a reaction uphill. If the far valley is higher, the net reaction runs the other way.

scenes.tts: So how does a protein lower the top? Its active site better matches the transition state than the substrate. It holds the substrate more loosely and the transition state more snugly.
scenes.visual: Restore the original landscape (right valley lower). On 'how does a protein' the camera eases onto the TEAL pass and the ENZYME arrives: a TEAL cup-shaped cleft whose inner hollow resembles, but does not exactly copy, the stretched PURPLE transition-state oval of s05. It fills about 60% of the frame height. On 'better matches' the PURPLE oval appears inside the hollow with small gaps and several GOLD contacts: a closer electrostatic and geometric match, not a perfect shape match. On 'substrate more loosely' a round YELLOW dot drops into the cup and rattles, with larger gaps and only two GOLD contact ticks. On 'more snugly' the dot stretches into the PURPLE oval and the cup's lips close a little; more GOLD contact ticks light around it (eight in total).
scenes.narration: So how does a protein lower the top? Its active site better matches the transition state than the substrate. It holds the substrate more loosely and the transition state more snugly.

scenes.tts: That extra grip pays back energy right at the top. The climb from the bound substrate shrinks. That bound-substrate speed-up equals how many times tighter it grips the transition state.
scenes.visual: Split frame: the cup on the left, a zoom of the TEAL pass on the right (x 0.5..6). On 'extra grip' the six extra GOLD ticks (beyond the substrate's two) detach as GOLD sparks and float to the right panel, where they land on the TEAL top and push it down a notch. On 'bound substrate' a YELLOW bracket from the bound-substrate level to the top shrinks as the top drops. On 'how many times tighter' a balance appears under the cup: 'grip on transition state' (PURPLE, 28) over 'grip on substrate' (YELLOW, 28) as a fraction, with '= speed-up' (TEAL, 30) beside it.
scenes.narration: That extra grip pays back energy right at the top. The climb from the bound substrate shrinks. That bound-substrate speed-up equals how many times tighter it grips the transition state.

scenes.tts: An active site that gripped the substrate just as hard would gain nothing. Both would sink together, and the climb would stay the same.
scenes.visual: Same split frame. On 'just as hard' the YELLOW dot in the cup gets all eight GOLD ticks too. In the right panel the bound-substrate level and the top sink by the same amount together (both lines move as one); the YELLOW bracket between them keeps exactly its length, and a 'no faster' chip (RED, 30) appears beside it. Then on 'stay the same' the extra ticks on the substrate fade back to two, ready for the return.
scenes.narration: An active site that gripped the substrate just as hard would gain nothing. Both would sink together, and the climb would stay the same.

scenes.tts: So the valleys decide which way a reaction runs. The ridge decides how fast. An enzyme touches only the ridge, by gripping the top hardest.
scenes.visual: Zoom back out to the full landscape as in s06: RED dashed high pass, TEAL lowered pass, both valleys pinned. On 'the valleys decide' both floors glow (YELLOW left, GREEN right) and the 'which way?' chip returns GREEN. On 'The ridge decides' the TEAL pass glows and the 'how fast?' chip returns RED. On 'gripping the top hardest' the small TEAL cup reappears at the TEAL top, closed snugly on a PURPLE oval with GOLD ticks, and dots stream over the pass in a steady flow.
scenes.narration: So the valleys decide which way a reaction runs. The ridge decides how fast. An enzyme touches only the ridge, by gripping the top hardest.

scenes.visual: End card over the living landscape at 20% opacity (dots still crossing the TEAL pass). LINE (TITLE_FONT 40): 'An enzyme lowers the ridge. It never moves the valleys.' Below it: biochemistrypedia.com (TEAL).
